A2_S4_D1: ^Oren: With the Great Disaster’s return upon us, what better time to retell the tale of the last flood?
^Oren: A tale of bravery and betrayal; of struggles and battles which changed the course of the world!
^Oren: A tale that began with just two people, and a boat.
^Oren: Once upon a time, a boy with a yearning heart was born in a distant land.
^Oren: His heart called for the great beyond — but his people shamed him for the foolish wish.
^Oren: For they believed their home was blessed. A land without creatures nor storms. A haven which may only be touched by the Great Floods.
^Oren: His people could not spare a moment for his dreams. And so, as time grew, so did his restlessness.
^Oren: Until one day, he departed his homeland with his closest ally and friend. And maybe a little more?
^Narrator: Oren winks, causing the crowd to huff out a laugh under their breaths.
^Oren: Together they sailed into the endless expanse. Mocked by their people and forbidden to return, they discovered joys and curiosities in the outside world.
^Oren: They discovered a world of creatures, and even landed on our Thavmian shores. Yes; they befriended many and learned from our vibrant, diverse strengths. Exchanging stories and skills.
^Oren: But of course; there was an imminent issue…
^Oren: The Great Disaster was due to come in a month.
^Narrator: The main protagonist is Noah, an idealist who hoped to share the knowledge of wayfaring with others and connect them across the seas.
^Narrator: While his best friend was Elio, a prodigy in sailing and building ships. A realist who’s loyal to those he holds dear..
^Narrator: After recounting more of the duo’s adventures, Oren wraps up the story on a cliffhanger; where Noah discovers that the Great Disaster was indeed a creature that could be found.
^Narrator: Not just a myth or turn of phrase. A real, breathing being, somewhere out in the seas.
^Oren: Do return tomorrow evening for the conclusion of our brave duo’s tale!
^Oren: I assure you, it’ll certainly be worth the wait.
^Narrator: Oren smiles and chats with the lingering audience, soaking in the attention as if he’s done it all his life.
^Chione: Hey, you two! How did you find the story?
^Narrator: Chione and Amaya appear from behind you. They must’ve been part of the standing crowd.
^Amelia: The story about this Noah guy is pretty popular. Even I’ve heard it before.
^Amelia: But… that stuff about his home island. Doesn’t it sound kind of familiar?
^Narrator: With all their eyes on you, you decide it’d be best not to lie, lest it gives them a reason to rescind their hospitality.
^Narrator: You tell them about our island, and how you fled from it recently due to their stance on creatures.
^Amaya: Can’t say I’ve heard of an island by that name. But due to the floods, many titles have also been changed and lost.
^Noelle: The Great Disaster… that’s what you guys call the creature behind the floods, right?
^Amaya: While Thavmia doesn’t get that many visitors, most people in the surrounding islands do call it by that name.
^Noelle: Is Thavmia the name of this island?
^Chione: Yes! It’s named after the unique evolution of humans on our land.
^Narrator: Chione gestures to her own features and Amaya’s.
^Chione: Due to how ancient Thavmia is, our human ancestors have since adapted to the regions they lived in over many generations.
^Chione: We Viridi live in the forest, while other settlements go by different names.
^Amaya: But aside from some biological evolution, we don’t have any special abilities. Not the kinds that Oren might make up for his stories, anyways.
^Noelle: I see… so there are other types of… uh.
^Amelia: Along with creatures, regular humans, and krakenfolk like you.
^Narrator: Amelia nudges your leg with an exasperated sigh.
^Amelia: What would you have done if we hadn’t run into each other?
^Narrator: Despite yourself, your lips quirk into a smile.
^Noelle: I guess I would’ve lived on berries until the Great Floods came.
^Chione: Well, you don’t have to do that now.
^Chione: But I wonder… could your homeland really be the same as Noah’s?
^Noelle: There might be other places that are similar in geography… But the odd thing is, I‘ve never heard of this ‘Noah’ before.
^Noelle: (That is, unless he was written out of our history books.)
^Chione: Is there anything else that’s different about your homeland?
^Narrator: Chione’s eyes have lit up excitedly.
^Chione: What kind of animals live there? What is the climate like?
^Narrator: Chione’s sudden flurry of questions take you by surprise, but her excitement motivates you to grapple for a satisfying answer.

^Noelle: Well, we only have regular humans there… Amelia’s actually the first creature I’ve met in my life. But I guess the climate is similar? Though ours is flatter and filled with more buildings than trees.
^Amaya: Speaking of climate… I’ve handed the artifact and ore from earlier to Silas. He’s agreed that we can supply you with some wood in return for your work.
^Amelia: Will we get to find out what the artifact’s about?
^Amaya: Hm… Probably, so long as it isn’t too sensitive. You did find it after all.
^Chione: We’ll probably have answers to that tomorrow!
^Amelia: Right… We’ve been running around all day.
^Amelia: It’s hard with my size, you know!
^Amaya: Well, so long as you’re willing to adapt and listen to the world around you, there are other ways of surviving the floods.
^Chione: Right! We’ll tell you more about how Thavmia prepares tomorrow, if you’d like.
^Amaya: Just go back and relax for now.
